title: Clock-free graphs are clean
statement_text: The class of clock-free graphs is clean.
context_text: A clock is a graph consisting of an induced cycle $C$ and a vertex not in $C$ with at least two non-adjacent neighbours in $C$. A class $\mathcal{C}$ of graphs is clean if there exists $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $t$, every $t$-clean graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$ satisfies $\mathrm{tw}(G)\leq f(t)$. The conjecture was posed in prior joint work [1] by Abrishami, Alecu, Chudnovsky, Hajebi, Spirkl, and Vušković, where a weaker version (for (clock, prism, pyramid)-free graphs) was proved.
attributed_to: Abrishami, Alecu, Chudnovsky, Hajebi, Spirkl, and Vušković
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture in full (Theorem 1.1): every clock-free graph of large treewidth contains, as an induced subgraph, one of the basic obstructions — a complete graph, a subdivision of a wall, or the line graph of a subdivision of a wall.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions XIV. Non-adjacent neighbours in a hole

title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: For every fixed $t \geq 1$, the family of $t$-clock-free graphs is clean.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, and $G$ is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The $t$-basic obstructions are $K_{t+1}$, $K_{t,t}$, subdivisions of the $(t\times t)$-wall, and line graphs of subdivisions of the $(t\times t)$-wall; all have treewidth $t$. A graph is $t$-clean if it contains no $t$-basic obstruction as an induced subgraph. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is clean if there is $f$ such that every $t$-clean graph in $\mathcal{C}$ has treewidth at most $f(t)$, i.e. large treewidth forces a large basic obstruction. The class of all graphs is not clean, because of Pohoata–Davies graphs, layered wheels and occultations, and neither is the class of wheel-free graphs. A hole is an induced cycle of length at least 4. A clock is a hole $C$ plus a vertex $v\notin C$ (its center) whose neighbours on $C$ include two non-adjacent vertices. A $t$-clock is a clock with two neighbours $x,y\in V(C)$ of $v$ at distance at least $t$ along $C$, so 2-clocks are exactly the clocks and the classes of $t$-clock-free graphs grow with $t$. Clocks appear in all three known non-basic constructions. Earlier, the authors and coauthors proved that (clock, prism, pyramid)-free graphs form a clean class. The main result of this paper is that the class of clock-free graphs is clean, which settles $t\le2$. The conjecture asserts the strengthening for every fixed $t$, where only clocks whose center has two neighbours far apart on the hole are excluded.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions XIV. Non-adjacent neighbours in a hole
